findings.priority_reason: Invoking ctx.exit() now automatically closes callbacks registered with call_on_close before raising Exit, changing cleanup timing for any application exit flow.
findings.title: Context exit triggers registered close callbacks
findings.before: def exit(self, code: int = 0) -> t.NoReturn: """Exits the application with a given exit code.""" raise Exit(code)
findings.after: def exit(self, code: int = 0) -> t.NoReturn: """Exits the application with a given exit code. .. versionchanged:: 8.2 Force closing of callbacks registered with :meth:`call_on_close` before exiting the CLI. """ self.close() raise Exit(code)
findings.scenario: A context with a registered close callback calls ctx.exit().
findings.example_before: ctx.exit(0) raises Exit(0) immediately without invoking the close callback.
findings.example_after: ctx.exit(0) invokes self.close() on the context, executing the registered close callback, then raises Exit(0).
findings.potential_impact: Resources managed via call_on_close will now be released during any call to ctx.exit() rather than surviving past context teardown initiated by exit.
findings.review_question: Do any existing callers rely on close callbacks deferring execution past an explicit ctx.exit() call?
